ELI5: Why do babies and little kids throw up so much?

Babies usually throw up because they can't burp on their own. When an adult swallows excess air while drinking, they burp. Babies can't without help. So if someone doesn't burp them, the pressure will upset their stomach, and their body has to find some way to release that pressure.

ELI5: Why is acid so bad for our teeth?

Your teeth, in essence, dissolve in the presence of acid. The minerals that make up your teeth dissolve in low pH solutions the same way salt dissolves in water.

Fluoride, on the other hand, encourages remineralization, and can help to slow this damage/repair it. This is why there is fluoride in tap water, toothpaste, your dentist puts it on your teeth, etc.

Most people don't realize this, but sugary foods themselves don't cause tooth decay. Your mouth is full of bacteria that feed on the sugars you eat, and excrete acid (lactic acid the most common culprit, IIRC).

I once heard a theory in college that some people who don't get dental carries managed to survive to a certain age without exposure to those bacteria, which were never able to establish a foothold. If you aren't exposed by a certain age, their immune system will be able to prevent them from taking hold and will consequently probably be cavity free their entire lives.
